title: Dev Sample v4 Rebuild + Universe Decision Record
summary: T0: branch/prompt/config committed. T1: D1 (analysis universe = in_scope=TRUE AND source_file='file1', 15,763 events) and D2 (clean_window is an eligibility flag for window-dependent measurements, not a universe filter - risk register #8) recorded verbatim to docs/Universe-Decisions.md; Open-Items-Register's implicit 2025-inclusion question formally closed referencing D1. T2: sampling frame built (15,763/15,349/414) and reconciled exactly against spine_window_flags.parquet's own file1 union/overlap (287/386/259-28-127). T3: located v3's sampling algorithm unambiguously (research/phase_3/build_dev_sample_v3.py, inline in main(), not an importable function) and replicated it verbatim for the v4 primary draw - 50 events, 10/10 deciles at 5 each, drawn twice within-process and confirmed byte-identical. T4: flagged sidecar drawn from 54 distinct bitmap patterns among the 414 flagged events - top 6 by frequency, one event each, also reproducible. T5: filtered_trades_dev_v4/filtered_quotes_dev_v4 materialized via spine join (not folder presence); v3 dev tables untouched; all 50 primary events have both trades and quotes rows; 3/6 sidecar events legitimately have 0 quotes rows (their picked pattern is quotes-side all-missing, the documented non-failing case); representative effective-spread query (ASOF join to prevailing quote, CLAUDE.md's cross-the-spread rule) ran in 17.1s, under the 60s ceiling. T6: representativeness chart built and kaleido-verified - primary cohort's ECDF tracks the frame closely, per-decile points span rather than cluster. T7: this digest and REPORT.md.

decisions_log.decision: Replicated v3's sampling algorithm verbatim in a new draw() function rather than importing/calling v3's main()
decisions_log.reason: v3's sampling logic (pd.qcut + np.random.default_rng loop) is inline in build_dev_sample_v3.py:main(), not factored into an importable function, and main() has side effects (writes config/dev_sample_v3.json, drops/recreates the v3 dev tables) that must not be re-triggered - copying the exact code (cited to the specific line range) satisfies 'reuse, don't reimplement from memory' without invoking v3's own write path

decisions_log.decision: Sidecar allocation used pandas value_counts() for pattern ranking (stable sort) rather than a custom tie-break rule
decisions_log.reason: 54 distinct patterns existed among the 414 flagged events, well above the 6 needed, so no tie-breaking or top-pattern-duplication fallback was actually exercised this run - value_counts()'s default descending-frequency order was sufficient

decisions_log.decision: Representative query used effective spread (ASOF join to the prevailing quote), not quoted spread
decisions_log.reason: CLAUDE.md's standing methodology: 'Effective spread, not quoted. Always cross the spread' - applied even though this is a runtime smoke test, not an analysis deliverable, since it is the query shape future window-dependent phases will actually run

surprises: 3 of the 6 flagged-sidecar events (APLD, NUKK, PSIX) have 0 quotes rows in filtered_quotes_dev_v4 - not a bug: their drawn pattern is quotes-side all-missing (e.g. 1111111|0000000), so 0 rows is the exact expected shape for that pattern, and T5a's presence check correctly does not fail on it (only primary-cohort absence is a failure condition).

The v4 primary cohort's momentum_pct range (decile 9: 110.45-259.85) sits entirely below the frame's and Phase 5's full-population max (918.26, from source_file='file2' - excluded under D1) - the clean file1 frame's own top decile tops out well short of that, a fact of the D1-scoped population, not a sampling artifact.

approval_gate: Do not begin Phase 6 scoping or any analysis work until Cooper has reviewed results and given explicit approval. On approval, tag phase-5a-approved. Dev sample v4 is then pinned - it does not change for the remainder of the program.
